questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere I had never been before and also where I knew I would be able to see a lot of nature without having to travel too far. Toronto is a nice and diverse city, but if I had to choose again I might have chosen a destination that was even closer to nature if possible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a nice time in general and everything went well, but the study system is very different from what I am used to, so I found it quite hard to find a proper 'flow' in how things worked study-wise over there.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I felt like I had to seek out information myself upon arrival instead of having someone helping you. We didn't get that much information about the system or how classes worked and all that stuff, so I had to ask around myself to learn that stuff.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got some assistance with switching my courses around when I first arrived, because I had some trouble with some of the courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy to find housing at all and I found it quite late compared to what I had wished for. It was okay, a little far out though. I wish we had more help to find housing. Find groups on Facebook and search online for housing - also maybe ask around if you know anybody that are also searching for something. It might be easier to find something when you are several people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: As long as you find something which is close to the subway, either line 1 or 2, you should be fine. It doesn't take that long to get to campus if you live close to a subway station seeing that campus is by one of the stations.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Its quite messy to register for the courses. Some courses are shown on one site as being held and another says that it isn't, so be carefull to double check that the courses you wish for is being held.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to see available courses at one website and then get them pre-approved. After this there were rounds for applying for the courses where you have to be precise when writing your prerequisites because you otherwise could be rejected from having the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I found help on campus after I had arrived, so they helped me in-person.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful but some courses were listed as in-person when they were actually online, which I did not think was okay at all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont take any online classes when you're on exchange.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two second-year courses and two fourth-year courses. I felt like the workload was big, but also because they had another style of teaching.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Amy second-year courses I felt like they had to make sure that we did everything properly and attended the classes etc. We weren't as 'free' to take responsibility for our own learning which I found quite annoying seeing that it sometimes felt like being treated like a kid.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EEB268, Plant and Microbial Diversity
PSL280, Introduction to Physiological Adaptions of Marine Mammals
PSL480, Diving Physiology of Marine Mammals
FOR413, Wildlife Ecology & Conservation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: FOR413, Wildlife Ecology & Conservation was my favorite course! Jennifer the professor is the best and sweetest teacher I've had in a long time and besides this she was very good at including present cases in her lectures, so it felt like there was a point to discussing the stuff we did in class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing big, but I was glad that I had my big winter boots and so on with me there.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing is very expensive and groceries are too.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything was available. I joined a running club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Running club was really nice - It was two days during the week and people were very sweet and you weren't obligated to show up.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Niagara Falls - take a day out of the calendar to go there by train. its very nice. I also went to Calgary, Banff and I wish I had more time there! It was incredible!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, everybody is very sweet and its all in English so its not that hard.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and say hi to people. If you have any questions then don't be afraid to ask them also to the local student. They often know things the best and they are most often very happy to help.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find anything that difficult with cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It is very diverse compared to Denmark and that was very nice to experience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open and ask the locals (maybe your classmates) what to see and do around the city. They often have good recommendations. 
Expect to be a bid stressed during the first month seeing that you need to settle in and find your way around. 
Exploit the time you have and say yes to as many experiences as possible. It worth the tiredness in the end.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you live close to campus it might be nice for you to buy a used bike instead of taking public transport.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friend you get out of it and everything that you see and experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Joggeling your time between having to do some school and wanting to see your friends and do social stuff most of the time can be a struggle.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
